# HIPAA Security Rule self-assessment of HIM Workbench

<!-- Generated by scripts/hipaa_assessment_cli.py --write. Do not edit by hand: a test fails if this file drifts from the code. -->

**Synthetic data only. A self-assessment by the author, not an audit, certification or legal advice.** HIPAA applies to covered entities and business associates handling real ePHI; this project handles none. The question here is what would have to be true before real ePHI went near it.

Each row is a standard or implementation specification from [45 CFR 164 Subpart C](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C), with (R) required or (A) addressable as the rule's own matrix gives it. Software cannot show organizational, workforce or physical measures, so those rows say **Organizational** instead of claiming they are met. Rows with automated checks are verified against the repo each time this is generated: if a check stops holding the status becomes **RE-CHECK**, including for "not met" rows.

## Result

| Status | Rows |
|---|---|
| Partly met | 10 |
| Not met | 7 |
| Not applicable | 6 |
| Organizational | 11 |

## Biggest technical gaps

- **164.312(a)(2)(i) Unique user identification** (Not met): No user identity anywhere. Nothing records or could record who did something.
- **164.312(d) Person or entity authentication** (Not met): Those checks are not authentication. Nothing verifies who is using the app.
- **164.312(a)(2)(iii) Automatic logoff** (Not met): No sessions, so nothing times out. Anyone at the unlocked computer has full access.
- **164.312(a)(2)(iv) Encryption and decryption (at rest)** (Not met): SQLite databases, the audit log and data files are plain files. Disk encryption (for example FileVault) would be an operating-system control that this repo cannot show.
- **164.312(b) Audit controls** (Partly met): No user identity in entries. The log is a plain file: nothing stops it being edited or deleted, and there is no rotation or retention rule.
- **164.312(c)(1)-(2) Mechanism to authenticate ePHI** (Partly met): No checksums or signatures on stored data. Anyone with file access can edit the databases directly.
- **164.312(e)(1) Integrity controls (A), encryption (A)** (Partly met): If the host binding were changed to a LAN address there would be no TLS. The SMART server URL can be overridden by an environment variable and is not forced to HTTPS in code, so an http:// override would send the bearer token in clear.

None of this is a flaw for a local, single-user, synthetic-data learning project. It is the list of what would need to be built or arranged first: user accounts and unique IDs, automatic logoff, encryption at rest, a tamper-resistant audit log that records who, backups, and the written policies around them.

## What is checked

Automated checks run against the repo for the rows above, for example: the server binds to 127.0.0.1, every request's Host header is verified, POSTs must be JSON, no authentication code exists, no encryption library is used, audit logging is called from many modules and tested never to hold patient values or questions, data and logs are gitignored, and the pre-commit hook scans for secrets. See `src/him_workbench/hipaa_assessment.py`.

## About the rule changing

HHS has proposed rewriting the Security Rule, including removing the required/addressable distinction so that currently addressable items become mandatory. As of mid-2026 reporting this is still a proposal, not a final rule, with a final rule targeted for July 2027. This table uses the current designations. For how to carry out each standard, NIST SP 800-66 Revision 2 is the guidance; a per-row crosswalk to it is not included here.
